messages:
jt-cust: Hey team — our prod tenant (tenant_id=acme-42) started getting 500s from the hosted inference API at ~09:10 UTC. All requests that previously worked are failing with a control-plane error: 'auth/session: upstream timeout' and an occasional 'routing-policy: configdb timeout'. See sample curl + response below.

jt-cust: ```
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"control-plane: auth/session error: timeout", "code":500}
```

amy-support: Thanks — sorry about that. Can you confirm correlation id or the full response headers if available? Any recent config changes or billing updates on your side? :thinking:

jt-cust: No config changes on our side. We did have a billing card rotation yesterday but that completed fine. Correlation id header: X-Request-ID=req_20260317_9921.

opcall-bot: :rotating_light: alert: control-plane.auth.session.timeouts spike 09:09:45 - 09:12:10, 82% error rate — paging sre oncall.

paul-sre: saw the same alert. Looking at control-plane metrics: auth-session service reported elevated connection timeouts to configdb replica set 10.1.3.7 between 09:08-09:14. Routing-policy service also shows increased p95 latency and some 502/503 cascades.

maria-platform: We have a recent small deploy of auth-cache refresh logic rolled out 09:05 UTC that touches session eviction. Can we confirm whether the new code path triggers a burst of configdb reads?

ev an-eng: I reproduced locally with a small load test and saw auth-service opening lots of short-lived connections to configdb and hitting maxConn. Repro steps I used: 

1) export REDWOOD_TENANT=acme-42
2) run: ```for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait```
Observed: 30-50% 500s from control-plane, logs show: `configdb: connection pool exhausted` and `auth/session: rpc timeout to routing-policy`.

amy-support: Great repro, thanks Evan. Can you share the auth-service logs around the error? Any stack traces?

ev an-eng: Pasted trimmed logs: ```
[09:10:02] auth-service WARN session_cache: eviction loop triggered, pool_wait_time=1200ms
[09:10:03] auth-service ERROR configdb: timeout acquiring connection after 1000ms
[09:10:04] routing-policy ERROR evaluate: upstream configdb timeout -> returning 500
```

paul-sre: Immediate mitigation: increased configdb connection pool size on control-plane nodes and bumped per-service max open connections. I also re-enabled an older auth-cache path (rollback of the eviction change) for the canary group. Monitoring now.

maria-platform: Noted. Also toggled routing-policy fallback to stateless-eval for the affected tenant to avoid configdb reads (temporary).

jt-cust: Thanks — errors dropped ~2m after your changes. Can you confirm root cause and next steps? Our SLA ticket is open.

amy-support: Root cause (prelim): recent auth-cache eviction change caused a surge of configdb reads under concurrent sessions which exhausted connection pools and produced cascading timeouts in routing-policy -> control-plane 500s.

ev an-eng: Follow-ups: (1) add circuit-breaker on auth->configdb path, (2) increase pool + connection backoff, (3) add synthetic monitoring for tenant-level configdb QPS, (4) run a small canary with the patched eviction algorithm and gradual rollouts.

paul-sre: Created incident follow-up ticket INF-2389 with action items, assigned to eng and platform. Will post postmortem link when ready. For now, marking as resolved for tenant acme-42.

amy-support: Closing loop with customer: jt-cust — we rolled a mitigation and saw request success return to normal at 09:12:30 UTC. We'll send timeline + postmortem once ready. Sorry for disruption and thanks for quick repro steps. :pray:

jt-cust: Appreciate the quick response, please include the billing team too if there are any quota/billing impacts.

amy-support: Will do.

oncall-bot: incident INF-2389 acknowledged by oncall@redwood, priority P2.
